profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Nashville - Franklin) is located at 4600 Carothers Parkway, Franklin, TN 37067. The operator publishes a footprint of 80000 square feet and 6 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HITRUST, ISO 27001, SSAE 18, HIPAA. Tennessee has about 60 data centers statewide, and Greater Nashville hosts more than a third of them, with about 13 facilities operational or under construction in the Nashville metro itself, plus a separate cluster of seven data centers, mostly operated by Meta, around Gallatin roughly 30 miles northeast, per WPLN's November 2025 reporting. Franklin, Brentwood, Berry Hill, and Murfreesboro each hold a handful of additional data center facilities beyond Nashville proper. Cushman & Wakefield's market analysis, cited in that reporting, describes power availability as the top site-selection factor for developers in the region, pointing to Tennessee Valley Authority's established power infrastructure, proximity to the Cumberland River for cooling, and Nashville's status as an "emerging market" positioned alongside Austin as a newer data-center hub distinct from established markets like Phoenix, Dallas, and Atlanta.

TVA, which supplies power across the Nashville region, said in 2026 that data center demand had climbed to 18% of its industrial load in 2025 and was projected to double regionally by 2030, prompting what CEO Don Moul called the largest capital program in TVA's history: 6.2 gigawatts of new generation, more than 3.7 gigawatts of it already under construction, including a 1.5-gigawatt gas plant at Cumberland City due online later in 2026, a 1.5-gigawatt gas complex near Kingston slated for 2027, a license extension through the mid-2050s for the 4-gigawatt Browns Ferry nuclear plant approved in December 2025, and a $400 million federal grant toward small modular reactors at the Clinch River site near Oak Ridge. TVA's service territory saw more than $6.6 billion in announced capital investment in fiscal 2025, per Utility Dive's reporting, with data centers cited as the dominant driver alongside population growth.

reading.body:
The Franklin campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity across 80,000 square feet, enough to run roughly 150 GPU-dense racks at 40 kW each or 600 enterprise racks at 10 kW each, depending on actual tenant workloads and power allocation choices the operator has not disclosed.

At 6 MW, this facility would be entirely consumed by a single large AI training cluster. That scale places it well below hyperscale data center benchmarks but sufficient to support substantial compute workloads if the operator has sized the building for that purpose. The operator's own facility page does not specify how power density is allocated or whether this building is currently oriented toward AI, general colocation, or regulated workloads.

The certification stack, SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITRUST, and ISO 27001, qualifies the facility for financial services and healthcare tenants. These are compliance prerequisites, not indicators of current use or performance. They mean the facility can house regulated workloads, not that it does.

Among 24 Tennessee facilities tracked here, only this one publishes IT capacity, so the state total of 6 MW reflects a single site, not the state's actual installed base. The ranking represents a data gap, not evidence of scale. Tennessee's data center footprint beyond this facility remains unquantified on published operator pages.
